verses.t: Yoshiyahu kept the Pesach to his Yahuah in Yahrushalayim; he killed the Pesach lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month,
having placed the kohanim according to their divisions, arrayed in their garments, in the heykal of Yahuah.

And he told the Levites, the heykal servants of Yasharal, that they should sanctify themselves to Yahuah and put the set-apart ark of Yahuah in the house which Shelomoh the king, the son of Dawiḏ, had built;
and he said, "You need no longer carry it upon your shoulders. Now worship Yahuah your Aluahim and serve his people Yasharal; and prepare yourselves by your families and kindred,

in accordance with the directions of Dawiḏ king of Yasharal and the magnificence of Shelomoh his son. Stand in order in the heykal according to the groupings of the fathers' houses of you Levites, who minister before your brethren the people of Yasharal,
and kill the Pesach lamb and prepare the sacrifices for your brethren, and keep the Pesach according to the mitsvah of Yahuah which was given to Mosheh."

And Yoshiyahu gave to the people who were present thirty thousand lambs and kids, and three thousand calves; these were given from the king's possessions, as he promised, to the people and the kohanim and Levites.
And Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Yahḥial, the chief officers of the heykal, gave to the kohanim for the Pesach two thousand six hundred sheep and three hundred calves.
And Yahkanyah and Shemaiah and Nethanal his brother, and Hashabiah and Ochial and Yoram, captains over thousands, gave the Levites for the Pesach five thousand sheep and seven hundred calves.
And this is what took place. The kohanim and the Levites, properly arrayed and having the unleavened bread, stood according to kindred
and the grouping of the fathers' houses, before the people, to make the offering to Yahuah as it is written in the book of Mosheh; this they did in the morning.
They roasted the Pesach lamb with fire, as required; and they boiled the sacrifices in brass pots and caldrons, with a pleasing odor,
and carried them to all the people. Afterward they prepared the Pesach for themselves and for their brethren the kohanim, the sons of Aharon,
because the kohanim were offering the fat until night; so the Levites prepared it for themselves and for their brethren the kohanim, the sons of Aharon.
And the heykal singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their place according to the arrangement made by Dawiḏ, and also Asaph, Zechariah, and Eddinus, who represented the king.
The gatekeepers were at each gate; no one needed to depart from his duties, for their brethren the Levites prepared the Pesach for them.
So the things that had to do with the sacrifices to Yahuah were accomplished that day: the Pesach was kept
and the sacrifices were offered on the mizbe'ach of Yahuah, according to the command of King Yoshiyahu.
And the people of Yasharal who were present at that time kept the Pesach and the feast of unleavened bread seven days.
No Pesach like it had been kept in Yasharal since the times of Shemu'al the naḇi;
none of the kings of Yasharal had kept such a Pesach as was kept by Yoshiyahu and the kohanim and Levites and the men of Yahuḏah and all of Yasharal who were dwelling in Yahrushalayim.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of Yoshiyahu this Pesach was kept
And the deeds of Yoshiyahu were upright in the sight of Yahuah, for his heart was full of set-apartness.

The events of his reign have been recorded in the past, concerning those who sinned and acted wickedly toward Yahuah beyond any other people or kingdom, and how they grieved Yahuah deeply, so that the words of Yahuah rose up against Yasharal.
After all these acts of Yoshiyahu, it happened that Pharaoh, king of Mitsrayim, went to make war at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Yoshiyahu went out against him.
And the king of Mitsrayim sent word to him saying, "What have we to do with each other, king of Yahuḏah?
I was not sent against you by Yahuah Aluahim, for my war is at the Euphrates. And now Yahuah is with me! Yahuah is with me, urging me on! Stand aside, and do not oppose Yahuah."
But Yoshiyahu did not turn back to his chariot, but tried to fight with him, and did not heed the words of Yahrmeyahu the naḇi from the mouth of Yahuah.
He joined battle with him in the plain of Megiddo, and the commanders came down against King Yoshiyahu.
And the king said to his servants, "Take me away from the battIe, for I am very weak." And immediately his servants took him out of the line of battIe.
And he got into his second chariot; and after he was brought back to Yahrushalayim he died, and was buried in the tomb of his fathers.

And in all Yahuḏah they mourned for Yoshiyahu. Yahrmeyahu the naḇi lamented for Yoshiyahu, and the principal men, with the women, have made lamentation for him to this day; it was ordained that this should always be done throughout the whole nation of Yasharal.

These things are written in the book of the histories of the kings of Yahuḏah; and every one of the acts of Yoshiyahu, and his splendor, and his understanding of the law of Yahuah, and the things that he had done before and these that are now told, are recorded in the book of the kings of Yasharal and Yahuḏah.
And the men of the nation took Yahkanyah the son of Yoshiyahu, who was twenty three years old, and made him king in succession to Yoshiyahu his father.
And he reigned three months in Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim. Then the king of Mitsrayim deposed him from reigning in Yahrushalayim,
and fined the nation a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
And the king of Mitsrayim made Yahhoyaqim his brother king of Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim.
Yahhoyaqim put the nobles in prison, and seized his brother Zarius and brought him up out of Mitsrayim.
Yahhoyaqim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign in Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim, and he did what was evil in the sight of Yahuah.
And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him, and bound him with a chain of brass and took him away to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also took some set-apart vessels of Yahuah, and carried them away, and stored them in his heykal in Babylon.
But the things that are reported about Yahhoyaqim and his uncleanness and impiety are written in the chronicles of the kings.
Jehoiachin his son became king in his stead; when he was made king he was eighteen years old,
and he reigned three months and ten days in Yahrushalayim. He did what was evil in the sight of Yahuah.
So after a year Nebuchadnezzar sent and removed him to Babylon, with the set-apart vessels of Yahuah,
and made Zedekiah king of Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim. Zedekiah was twenty-one years old, and he reigned eleven years.
He also did what was evil in the sight of Yahuah, and did not heed the words that were spoken by Yahrmeyahu the naḇi from the mouth of Yahuah.

And though King Nebuchadnezzar had made him swear by the name of Yahuah, he broke his oath and rebelled; and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart and transgressed the laws of Yahuah, the Aluahim of Yasharal.

Even the leaders of the people and of the kohanim committed many acts of sacrilege and lawlessness beyond all the unclean deeds of all the nations, and polluted the heykal of Yahuah which had been hallowed in Yahrushalayim.
So the Aluahim of their fathers sent by his mal'ak to call them back, because he would have spared them and his dwelling place.
But they mocked his mal'akim, and whenever Yahuah spoke, they scoffed at his neḇi'im,
until in his anger against his people because of their ungodly acts he gave command to bring against them the kings of the Chaldeans.
These slew their young men with the sword around their set-apart heykal, and did not spare young man or virgin, old man or child, for he gave them all into their hands.
And all the set-apart vessels of Yahuah, great and small, and the treasure chests of Yahuah, and the royal stores, they took and carried away to Babylon.
And they burned the house of Yahuah and broke down the walls of Yahrushalayim and burned their towers with fire,
and utterly destroyed all its glorious things. The survivors he led away to Babylon with the sword,
and they were servants to him and to his sons until the Persians began to reign, in fulfillment of the word of Yahuah by the mouth of Yahrmeyahu:
"Until the land has enjoyed its Shabbaths, it shall keep Shabbath all the time of its desolation until the completion of seventy years."
In the first year of Cyrus as king of the Persians, that the word of Yahuah by the mouth of Yahrmeyahu might be accomplished,
Yahuah stirred up the ruach of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom and also put it in writing:
"Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: Yahuah of Yasharal, Yahuah Most High, has made me king of the world,
and he has commanded me to build him a house at Yahrushalayim, which is in Yahuḏah.

If any one of you, therefore, is of his people, may his Yahuah be with him, and let him go up to Yahrushalayim, which is in Yahuḏah, and build the house of Yahuah of Yasharal – he is Yahuah who dwells in Yahrushalayim,
and let each man, wherever he may live, be helped by the men of his place with gold and silver,
with gifts and with horses and cattle, besides the other things added as votive offerings for the heykal of Yahuah which is in Yahrushalayim."

Then arose the heads of families of the tribes of Yahuḏah and Binyamin, and the kohanim and the Levites, and all whose ruach Yahuah had stirred to go up to build the house in Yahrushalayim for Yahuah;
and their neighbors helped them with everything, with silver and gold, with horses and cattle, and with a very great number of votive offerings from many whose hearts were stirred.
Cyrus the king also brought out the set-apart vessels of Yahuah which Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Yahrushalayim and stored in his heykal of idols.
When Cyrus king of the Perians brought these out, he gave them to Mithridates his treasurer,
and by him they were given to Sheshbazzar the governor of Yahuḏah.
The number of these was: a thousand gold cups, a thousand silver cups, twenty-nine silver censers, thirty gold bowls, two thousand four hundred and ten silver bowls, and a thousand other vessels.
All the vessels were handed over, gold and silver, five thousand four hundred and sixty-nine,
and they were carried back by Sheshbazzar with the returning exiles from Babylon to Yahrushalayim.

But in the time of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Bishlam, Mithridates, Tabeal, Rehum, Beltethmus, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates, living in Samaria and other places, wrote him the following letter, against those who were living in Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim:
"To King Artaxerxes our Yahuah, Your servants Rehum the recorder and Shimshai the scribe and the other judges of their council in Coelesyria and Phoenicia:

Now be it known to our Yahuah the king that the Yahuḏim who came up from you to us have gone to Yahrushalayim and are building that rebellious and wicked city, repairing its market places and walls and laying the foundations for a heykal.
Now if this city is built and the walls finished, they will not only refuse to pay tribute but will even resist kings.
And since the building of the heykal is now going on, we think it best not to neglect such a matter,
but to speak to our Yahuah the king, in order that, if it seems good to you, search may be made in the records of your fathers.
You will find in the chronicles what has been written about them, and will learn that this city was rebellious, troubling both kings and other cities,
and that the Yahuḏim were rebels and kept setting up blockades in it from of old. That is why this city was laid waste.
Therefore we now make known to you, O Yahuah and king, that if this city is built and its walls finished, you will no longer have access to Coelesyria and Phoenicia."
Then the king, in reply to Rehum the recorder and Beltethmus and Shimshai the scribe and the others associated with them and living in Samaria and Syria and Phoenicia, wrote as follows:
"1 have read the letter which you sent me. So I ordered search to be made, and it has been found that this city from of old has fought against kings,
and that the men in it were given to rebellion and war, and that mighty and cruel kings ruled in Yahrushalayim and exacted tribute from Coelesyria and Phoenicia.
Therefore I have now issued orders to prevent these men from building the city and to take care that nothing more be done
and that such wicked proceedings go no further to the annoyance of kings."

Then, when the letter from King Artaxerxes was read, Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their associates went in haste to Yahrushalayim, with horsemen and a multitude in battle array, and began to hinder the builders. And the building of the heykal in Yahrushalayim ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
Now King Darius gave a great banquet for all that were under him and all that were born in his house and all the nobles of Media and Persia
and all the satraps and generals and governors that were under him in the hundred and twenty-seven satrapies from India to Ethiopia.
They ate and drank, and when they were satisfied they departed; and Darius the king went to his bedroom, and went to sleep, and then awoke.
Then the three young men of the bodyguard, who kept guard over the person of the king, said to one another,
"Let each of us state what one thing is strongest; and to him whose statement seems wisest, Darius the king will give rich gifts and great honors of victory.
He shall be clothed in purple, and drink from gold cups, and sleep on a gold bed, and have a chariot with gold bridles, and a turban of fine linen, and a necklace about his neck;
and because of his wisdom he shall sit next to Darius and shall be called kinsman of Darius."
Then each wrote his own statement, and they sealed them and put them under the pillow of Darius the king,

and said, "When the king wakes, they will give him the writing; and to the one whose statement the king and the three nobles of Persia judge to be wisest the victory shall be given according to what is written."
The first wrote, "Wine is strongest."
The second wrote, "The king is strongest."
The third wrote, "Women are strongest, but truth is victor over all things."
When the king awoke, they took the writing and gave it to him, and he read it.
Then he sent and summoned all the nobles of Persia and Media and the satraps and generals and governors and prefects,
and he took his seat in the council chamber, and the writing was read in their presence.
And he said, "Call the young men, and they shall explain their statements." So they were summoned, and came in.
And they said to them, "Explain to us what you have written." Then the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine, began and said:
"Gentlemen, how is wine the strongest? It leads astray the minds of all who drink it.
It makes equal the mind of the king and the orphan, of the slave and the free, of the poor and the rich.
It turns every thought to feasting and mirth, and forgets all sorrow and debt.
It makes all hearts feel rich, forgets kings and satraps, and makes every one talk in millions.
When men drink they forget to be friendly with friends and brothers, and before long they draw their swords.
And when they recover from the wine, they do not remember what they have done.
Gentlemen, is not wine the strongest, since it forces men to do these things?" When he had said this, he stopped speaking.
Then the second, who had spoken of the strength of the king, began to speak:
"Gentlemen, are not men strongest, who rule over land and sea and all that is in them?
But the king is stronger; he is their Yahuah and master, and whatever he says to them they obey.
If he tells them to make war on one another, they do it; and if he sends them out against the enemy, they go, and conquer mountains, walls, and towers.
They kill and are killed, and do not disobey the king's command; if they win the victory, they bring everything to the king – whatever spoil they take and everything else.
Likewise those who do not serve in the army or make war but till the soil, whenever they sow, reap the harvest and bring some to the king; and they compel one another to pay taxes to the king.
And yet he is only one man! If he tells them to kill, they kill; if he tells them to release, they release;
if he tells them to attack, they attack; if he tells them to lay waste, they lay waste; if he tells them to build, they build;
if he tells them to cut down, they cut down; if he tells them to plant, they plant.
All his people and his armies obey him. Moreover, he reclines, he eats and drinks and sleeps,
but they keep watch around him and no one may go away to attend to his own affairs, nor do they disobey him.
Gentlemen, why is not the king the strongest, since he is to be obeyed in this fashion?" And he stopped speaking.
Then the third, that is Zerubbabal, who had spoken of women and truth, began to speak:
Gentlemen, is not the king great, and are not men many, and is not wine strong? Who then is their master, or who is their Yahuah? Is it not women?
Women gave birth to the king and to every people that rules over sea and land.
From women they came; and women brought up the very men who plant the vineyards from which comes wine.
Women make men's clothes; they bring men glory; men cannot exist without women.
If men gather gold and silver or any other beautiful thing, and then see a woman lovely in appearance and beauty,
they let all those things go, and gape at her, and with open mouths stare at her, and all prefer her to gold or silver or any other beautiful thing.
A man leaves his own father, who brought him up, and his own country, and cleaves to his wife.
With his wife he ends his days, with no thought of his father or his mother or his country.
Hence you must realize that women rule over you! "Do you not labor and toil, and bring everything and give it to women?
A man takes his sword, and goes out to travel and rob and steal and to sail the sea and rivers;
he faces lions, and he walks in darkness, and when he steals and robs and plunders, he brings it back to the woman he loves.
A man loves his wife more than his father or his mother.
Many men have lost their minds because of women, and have become slaves because of them.
Many have perished, or stumbled, or sinned, because of women.
And now do you not believe me? "Is not the king great in his power? Do not all lands fear to touch him?
Yet I have seen him with Apame, the king's concubine, the daughter of the illustrious Bartacus; she would sit at the king's right hand
and take the crown from the king's head and put it on her own, and slap the king with her left hand.
At this the king would gaze at her with mouth agape. If she smiles at him, he laughs; if she loses her temper with him, he flatters her, that she may be reconciled to him.
Gentlemen, why are not women strong, since they do such things?"
Then the king and the nobles looked at one another; and he began to speak about truth:
"Gentlemen, are not women strong? The earth is vast, and shamayim is high, and the sun is swift in its course, for it makes the circuit of the shamayim and returns to its place in one day.
Is he not great who does these things? But truth is great, and stronger than all things.
The whole earth calls upon truth, and shamayim blesses her. All Aluahim's works quake and tremble, and with him there is nothing unrighteous.

Wine is unrighteous, the king is unrighteous, women are unrighteous, all the sons of men are unrighteous, all their works are unrighteous, and all such things. There is no truth in them and in their unrighteousness they will perish.
But truth endures and is strong for ever, and lives and prevails for ever and ever.
With her there is no partiality or preference, but she does what is righteous instead of anything that is unrighteous or wicked. All men approve her deeds,
and there is nothing unrighteous in her mishpat. To her belongs the strength and the kingship and the power and the majesty of all the ages. Baruk be the Aluahim of truth!"
He ceased speaking; then all the people shouted, and said, "Great is truth, and strongest of all!"

Then the king said to him, "Ask what you wish, even beyond what is written, and we will give it to you, for you have been found to be the wisest. And you shall sit next to me, and be called my kinsman."
Then he said to the king, "Remember the vow which you made to build Yahrushalayim, in the day when you became king,
and to send back all the vessels that were taken from Yahrushalayim, which Cyrus set apart when he began to destroy Babylon, and vowed to send them back there.
You also vowed to build the heykal, which the Edomites burned when Yahuḏah was laid waste by the Chaldeans.

And now, O Yahuah the king, this is what I ask and request of you, and this befits your greatness. I pray therefore that you fulfil the vow whose fulfilment you vowed to the King of shamayim with your own lips."

Then Darius the king rose, and kissed him, and wrote letters for him to all the treasurers and governors and generals and satraps, that they should give escort to him and all who were going up with him to build Yahrushalayim.
And he wrote letters to all the governors in Coelesyria and Phoenicia and to those in Lebanon, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to Yahrushalayim, and to help him build the city.
And he wrote for all the Yahuḏim who were going up from his kingdom to Yahuḏah, in the interest of their freedom, that no officer or satrap or governor or treasurer should forcibly enter their doors;
that all the country which they would occupy should be theirs without tribute; that the Idumeans should give up the villages of the Yahuḏim which they held;

that twenty talents a year should be given for the building of the heykal until it was completed, and an additional ten talents a year for burnt offerings to be offered on the mizbe'ach every day, in accordance with the mitsvah to make seventeen offerings; and that all who came from Babylonia to build the city should have their freedom, they and their children and all the kohanim who came. He wrote also concerning their support and the kohanim' garments in which they were to minister.

He wrote that the support for the Levites should be provided until the day when the heykal should be finished and Yahrushalayim built. He wrote that land and wages should be provided for all who guarded the city. And he sent back from Babylon all the vessels which Cyrus had set apart; everything that Cyrus had ordered to be done, he also commanded to be done and to be sent to Yahrushalayim.
When the young man went out, he lifted up his face to shamayim toward Yahrushalayim, and praised the King of shamayim, saying,
"From thee is the victory; from thee is wisdom, and your is the glory. I am thy servant.
Baruk art thou, who hast given me wisdom; I give thee thanks, O Yahuah of our fathers."
So he took the letters, and went to Babylon and told this to all his brethren.
And they praised the Aluahim of their fathers, because he had given them release and permission
to go up and build Yahrushalayim and the heykal which is called by his name; and they feasted, with music and rejoicing, for seven days.
After this the heads of fathers' houses were chosen to go up, according to their tribes, with their wives and sons and daughters, and their menservants and maidservants, and their cattle.
And Darius sent with them a thousand horsemen to take them back to Yahrushalayim in safety, with the music of drums and flutes;
and all their brethren were making merry. And he made them go up with them.
These are the names of the men who went up, according to their fathers' houses in the tribes, over their groups:

the kohanim, the sons of Phinehas, son of Aharon; Jeshua the son of Jozadak, son of Seraiah, and Yoaqim the son of Zerubbabal, son of Shealtial, of the house of Dawiḏ, of the lineage of Phares, of the tribe of Yahuḏah,
who spoke wise words before Darius the king of the Persians, in the second year of his reign, in the month of Nisan, the first month.
These are the men of Yahuḏah who came up out of their sojourn in captivity, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away to Babylon

and who returned to Yahrushalayim and the rest of Yahuḏah, each to his own town. They came with Zerubbabal and Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Resaiah, Bigvai, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Reeliah, Rehum, and Baanah, their leaders.
The number of the men of the nation and their leaders: the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two. The sons of Shephatiah, four hundred and seventy-two.
The sons of Arah, seven hundred and fifty-six.
The sons of Pahathmoab, of the sons of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve.
The sons of Alam, one thousand two hundred and fifty four. The sons of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five. The sons of Chorbe, seven hundred and five. The sons of Bani, six hundred and forty-eight.
The sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three. The sons of Azgad, one thousand three hundred and twenty-two.
The sons of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-seven. The sons of Bigvai, two thousand and sixty-six. The sons of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four.
The sons of Ater, namely of Hezekiah, ninety-two. The sons of Kilan and Azetas, sixty-seven. The sons of Azaru, four hundred and thirty-two.
The sons of Annias, one hundred and one. The sons of Arom. The sons of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-three. The sons of Jorah, one hundred and twelve.
The sons of Baiterus, three thousand and five. The sons of Bethlehem, one hundred and twenty-three.
The men of Netophah, fifty-five. The men of Anathoth, one hundred and fifty-eight. The men of Bethasmoth, forty-two.
The men of Kiriatharim, twenty-five. The men of Chephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three.
The Chadiasans and Ammidians, four hundred and twenty-two. The men of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one.
The men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two. The men of Bethal, fifty-two. The sons of Magbish, one hundred and fifty-six.
The sons of the other Alam and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five. The sons of Yahriḥo, three hundred and forty-five.
The sons of Senaah, three thousand three hundred and thirty.
The kohanim: the sons of Jedaiah the son of Jeshua, of the sons of Anasib, nine hundred and seventy-two. The sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two.
The sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven. The sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmial and Bannas and Sudias, seventy-four.
The heykal singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and twenty-eight.
The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai, in all one hundred and thirty-nine.
The heykal servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth, the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Pad on, the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah,
the sons of Akkub, the sons of Uthai, the sons of Ketab, the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shamlai, the sons of Hana, the sons of Cathua, the sons of Gahar,

The sons of Reaiah, the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Chezib, the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Hasrah, the sons of Besai, the sons of Asnah, the sons of the Meunites, the sons of Nephisim, the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Asur, the sons of Pharakim, the sons of Bazluth,
the sons of Mehida, the sons of Cutha, the sons of Charea, the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah, the sons of Neziah, the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of Shelomoh's servants: the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Peruda, the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Lozon, the sons of Giddal, the sons of Shephatiah,

the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the sons of Sarothie, the sons of Masiah, the sons of Gas, the sons of Addus, the sons of Subas, the sons of Apherra, the sons of Barodis, the sons of Shaphat, the sons of Ami.
All the heykal servants and the sons of Shelomoh's servants were three hundred and seventy-two.
The following are those who came up from Telmelah and Telharsha, under the leadership of Cherub, Addan, and Immer,
though they could not prove by their fathers' houses or lineage that they belonged to Yasharal: the sons of Delaiah the son of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and fifty-two.

Of the kohanim the following had assumed the kehunnah but were not found registered: the sons of Habaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Jaddus who had married Agia, one of the daughters of Barzillai, and was called by his name.
And when the genealogy of these men was sought in the register and was not found, they were excluded from serving as kohanim.
And Nehemiah and Attharias told them not to share in the set-apart things until a kohen gadol should appear wearing Urim and Thummim.
All those of Yasharal, twelve or more years of age, besides menservants and maidservants, were forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty;
their menservants and maidservants were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; there were two hundred and forty-five musicians and singers.
There were four hundred and thirty-five camels, and seven thousand and thirty-six horses, two hundred and forty-five mules, and five thousand five hundred and twenty-five asses.
Some of the heads of families, when they came to the heykal of Aluahim which is in Yahrushalayim, vowed that they would erect the house on its site, to the best of their ability,
and that they would give to the sacred treasury for the work a thousand minas of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred kohanim' garments.
The kohanim, the Levites, and some of the people settled in Yahrushalayim and its vicinity; and the heykal singers, the gatekeepers, and all Yasharal in their towns.
When the seventh month came, and the sons of Yasharal were each in his own home, they gathered as one man in the square before the first gate toward the east.
Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak, with his fellow kohanim, and Zerubbabal the son of Shealtial, with his kinsmen, took their places and prepared the mizbe'ach of the Aluahim of Yasharal,
to offer burnt offerings upon it, in accordance with the directions in the book of Mosheh the man of Aluahim.

And some joined them from the other peoples of the land. And they erected the mizbe'ach in its place, for all the peoples of the land were hostile to them and were stronger than they; and they offered sacrifices at the proper times and burnt offerings to Yahuah morning and evening.
They kept the feast of booths, as it is commanded in the law, and offered the proper sacrifices every day,
and thereafter the continual offerings and sacrifices on Shabbaths and at new moons and at all the consecrated feasts.
And all who had made any vow to Aluahim began to offer sacrifices to Aluahim, from the new moon of the seventh month, though the heykal of Aluahim was not yet built.
And they gave money to the masons and the carpenters, and food and drink

and carts to the Sidonians and the Tyrians, to bring cedar logs from Lebanon and convey them in rafts to the harbor of Joppa, according to the decree which they had in writing from Cyrus king of the Persians.

In the second year after their coming to the heykal of Aluahim in Yahrushalayim, in the second month, Zerubbabal the son of Shealtial and Jeshua the son of Jozadak made a beginning, together with their brethren and the Levitical kohanim and all who had come to Yahrushalayim from the captivity;
and they laid the foundation of the heykal of Aluahim on the new moon of the second month in the second year after they came to Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim.

And they appointed the Levites who were twenty or more years of age to have charge of the work of Yahuah. And Jeshua arose, and his sons and brethren and Kadmial his brother and the sons of Jeshua Emadabun and the sons of Joda son of Iliadun, with their sons and brethren, all the Levites, as one man pressing forward the work on the house of Aluahim. So the builders built the heykal of Yahuah.
And the kohanim stood arrayed in their garments, with musical instruments and trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals,
praising Yahuah and berakah him, according to the directions of Dawiḏ king of Yasharal;
and they sang hymns, giving thanks to Yahuah, because his goodness and his glory are for ever upon all Yasharal.
And all the people sounded trumpets and shouted with a great shout, praising Yahuah for the erection of the house of Yahuah.
Some of the Levitical kohanim and heads of fathers' houses, old men who had seen the former house, came to the building of this one with outcries and loud weeping,
while many came with trumpets and a joyful noise,
so that the people could not hear the trumpets because of the weeping of the people. For the multitude sounded the trumpets loudly, so that the sound was heard afar;
and when the enemies of the tribe of Yahuḏah and Binyamin heard it, they came to find out what the sound of the trumpets meant.
And they learned that those who had returned from captivity were building the heykal for Yahuah Aluahim of Yasharal.
So they approached Zerubbabal and Jeshua and the heads of the fathers' houses and said to them, "We will build with you.
For we obey your Yahuah just as you do and we have been sacrificing to him ever since the days of Esarhaddon king of the Assyrians, who brought us here."
But Zerubbabal and Jeshua and the heads of the fathers' houses in Yasharal said to them, "You have nothing to do with us in building the house for Yahuah our Aluahim,
for we alone will build it for Yahuah of Yasharal, as Cyrus the king of the Persians has commanded us."
But the peoples of the land pressed hard upon those in Yahuḏah, cut off their supplies, and hindered their building;
and by plots and demagoguery and uprisings they prevented the completion of the building as long as King Cyrus lived. And they were kept from building for two years, until the reign of Darius.

Now in the second year of the reign of Darius, the neḇi'im Haggai and Zechariah the son of Iddo prophesied to the Yahuḏim who were in Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim, they prophesied to them in the name of Yahuah Aluahim of Yasharal.
Then Zerubbabal the son of Shealtial and Jeshua the son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of Yahuah which is in Yahrushalayim, with the help of the neḇi'im of Yahuah who were with them.
At the same time Sisinnes the governor of Syria and Phoenicia and Sathrabuzanes and their associates came to them and said,
"By whose order are you building this house and this roof and finishing all the other things? And who are the builders that are finishing these things?"
Yet the elders of the Yahuḏim were dealt with kindly, for the providence of Yahuah was over the captives;
and they were not prevented from building until word could be sent to Darius concerning them and a report made.
A copy of the letter which Sisinnes the governor of Syria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes, and their associates the local rulers in Syria and Phoenicia, wrote and sent to Darius:

"To King Darius, greeting. Let it be fully known to our Yahuah the king that, when we went to the country of Yahuḏah and entered the city of Yahrushalayim, we found the elders of the Yahuḏim, who had been in captivity,
building in the city of Yahrushalayim a great new house for Yahuah, of hewn stone, with costly timber laid in the walls.
These operations are going on rapidly, and the work is prospering in their hands and being completed with all splendor and care.
Then we asked these elders, 'At whose command are you building this house and laying the foundations of this structure?'
And in order that we might inform you in writing who the leaders are, we questioned them and asked them for a list of the names of those who are at their head.
They answered us, 'We are the servants of Yahuah who created the shamayim and the earth.
And the house was built many years ago by a king of Yasharal who was great and strong, and it was finished.
But when our fathers sinned against Yahuah of Yasharal who is in shamayim, and provoked him, he gave them over into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of the Chaldeans;
and they pulled down the house, and burned it, and carried the people away captive to Babylon.
But in the first year that Cyrus reigned over the country of Babylonia, King Cyrus wrote that this house should be rebuilt.

And the set-apart vessels of gold and of silver, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the house in Yahrushalayim and stored in his own heykal, these Cyrus the king took out again from the heykal in Babylon, and they were delivered to Zerubbabal and Sheshbazzar the governor
with the command that he should take all these vessels back and put them in the heykal at Yahrushalayim, and that this heykal of Yahuah should be rebuilt on its site.

Then this Sheshbazzar, after coming here, laid the foundations of the house of Yahuah which is in Yahrushalayim, and although it has been in process of construction from that time until now, it has not yet reached completion.'
Now therefore, if it seems wise, O king, let search be made in the royal archives of our Yahuah the king that are in Babylon;

and if it is found that the building of the house of Yahuah in Yahrushalayim was done with the consent of King Cyrus, and if it is approved by our Yahuah the king, let him send us directions concerning these things."

Then Darius commanded that search be made in the royal archives that were deposited in Babylon. And in Ecbatana, the fortress which is in the country of Media, a scroll was found in which this was recorded:
"In the first year of the reign of Cyrus, King Cyrus ordered the building of the house of Yahuah in Yahrushalayim, where they sacrifice with perpetual fire;
its height to be sixty cubits and its breadth sixty cubits, with three courses of hewn stone and one course of new native timber; the cost to be paid from the treasury of Cyrus the king;

and that the set-apart vessels of the house of Yahuah, both of gold and of silver, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of the house in Yahrushalayim and carried away to Babylon, should be restored to the house in Yahrushalayim, to be placed where they had been."

So Darius commanded Sisinnes the governor of Syria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes, and their associates, and those who were appointed as local rulers in Syria and Phoenicia, to keep away from the place, and to permit Zerubbabal, the servant of Yahuah and governor of Yahuḏah, and the elders of the Yahuḏim to build this house of Yahuah on its site.
"And I command that it be built completely, and that full effort be made to help the men who have returned from the captivity of Yahuḏah, until the house of Yahuah is finished;
and that out of the tribute of Coelesyria and Phoenicia a portion be scrupulously given to these men, that is, to Zerubbabal the governor, for sacrifices to Yahuah, for bulls and rams and lambs,
and likewise wheat and salt and wine and oil, regularly every year, without quibbling, for daily use as the kohanim in Yahrushalayim may indicate,
in order that libations may be made to the Most High Aluahim for the king and his children, and prayers be offered for their life."

And he commanded that if any should transgress or nullify any of the things herein written, a beam should be taken out of his house and he should be hanged upon it, and his property should be forfeited to the king.
"Therefore may Yahuah, whose name is there called upon, destroy every king and nation that shall stretch out their hands to hinder or damage that house of Yahuah in Yahrushalayim.
"I, King Darius, have decreed that it be done with all diligence as here prescribed. "
Then 5isinnes the governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia, and 5athrabuzanes, and their associates, following the orders of King Darius,
supervised the set-apart work with very great care, assisting the elders of the Yahuḏim and the chief officers of the heykal.
And the set-apart work prospered, while the neḇi'im Haggai and Zechariah prophesied;
and they completed it by the command of Yahuah Aluahim of Yasharal. 50 with the consent of Cyrus and Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of the Persians,
the set-apart house was finished by the twenty-third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of King Darius.
And the people of Yasharal, the kohanim, the Levites, and the rest of those from the captivity who joined them, did according to what was written in the book of Mosheh.
They offered at the dedication of the heykal of Yahuah one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs,
and twelve he-goats for the sin of all Yasharal, according to the number of the twelve leaders of the tribes of Yasharal;

and the kohanim and the Levites stood arrayed in their garments, according to kindred, for the services of Yahuah Aluahim of Yasharal in accordance with the book of Mosheh; and the gatekeepers were at each gate.
The people of Yasharal who came from the captivity kept the Pesach on the fourteenth day of the first month, after the kohanim and the Levites were purified together.
Not all of the returned captives were purified, but the Levites were all purified together,
and they sacrificed the Pesach lamb for all the returned captives and for their brethren the kohanim and for themselves.
And the people of Yasharal who came from the captivity ate it, all those who had separated themselves from the abominations of the peoples of the land and sought Yahuah.
And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, rejoicing before Yahuah,
Because he had changed the will of the king of the Assyrians concerning them, to strengthen their hands for the service of Yahuah Aluahim of Yasharal.
After these things, when Artaxerxes the king of the Persians was reigning, Ezra came, the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah, son of5hallum,
son of Zadok, son of Ahitub, son of Amariah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki, son of Abishua, son of Phineas, son of Aleazar, son of Aharon the chief kohen.
This Ezra came up from Babylon as a scribe skilled in the law of Mosheh, which was given by the Aluahim of Yasharal;
and the king showed him honor, for he found chen before the king in all his requests.
There came up with him to Yahrushalayim some of the people of Yasharal and some of the kohanim and Levites and heykal singers and gatekeepers and heykal servants,

in the seventh year of the reign of Artaxerxes, in the fifth month (this was the king's seventh year); for they left Babylon on the new moon of the first month and arrived in Yahrushalayim on the new moon of the fifth month, by the prosperous journey which Yahuah gave them.
For Ezra possessed great knowledge, so that he omitted nothing from the law of Yahuah or the mitsvot, but taught all Yasharal all the ordinances and mishpatim.
The following is a copy of the written commission from Artaxerxes the king which was delivered to Ezra the kohen and reader of the law of Yahuah:
"King Artaxerxes to Ezra the kohen and reader of the law of Yahuah, greeting.

In accordance with my gracious decision, I have given orders that those of the Yahuḏite nation and of the kohanim and Levites and others in our realm, who freely choose to do so, may go with you to Yahrushalayim.
Let as many as are so disposed, therefore, depart with you as I and the seven friends who are my counselors have decided,
in order to look into matters in Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim, in accordance with what is in the law of Yahuah,

and to carry to Yahrushalayim the gifts for Yahuah of Yasharal which I and my friends have vowed, and to collect for Yahuah in Yahrushalayim all the gold and silver that may be found in the country of Babylonia,
together with what is given by the nation for the heykal of their Yahuah which is in Yahrushalayim, both gold and silver for bulls and rams and lambs and what goes with them,
so as to offer sacrifices upon the mizbe'ach of their Yahuah which is in Yahrushalayim.
And whatever you and your brethren are minded to do with the gold and silver, perform it in accordance with the will of your Aluahim;
and deliver the set-apart vessels of Yahuah which are given you for the use of the heykal of your Aluahim which is in Yahrushalayim.
And whatever else occurs to you as necessary for the heykal of your Aluahim, you may provide out of the royal treasury.

"And I, Artaxerxes the king, have commanded the treasurers of Syria and Phoenicia that whatever Ezra the kohen and reader of the law of the Most High Aluahim sends for, they shall take care to give him,
up to a hundred talents of silver, and likewise up to a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, and salt in abundance.
Let all things prescribed in the law of Aluahim be scrupulously fulfilled for the Most High Aluahim, so that wrath may not come upon the kingdom of the king and his sons.

You are also informed that no tribute or any other tax is to be laid on any of the kohanim or Levites or heykal singers or gatekeepers or heykal servants or persons employed in this heykal, and that no one has authority to impose any tax upon them.

"And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of Aluahim, appoint judges and justices to judge all those who know the law of your Aluahim, throughout all Syria and Phoenicia; and those who do not know it you shall teach.
And all who transgress the law of your Aluahim or the law of the kingdom shall be strictly punished, whether by death or some other punishment, either fine or imprisonment."
Baruk be Yahuah alone, who put this into the heart of the king, to glorify his house which is in Yahrushalayim,
and who honored me in the sight of the king and his counselors and all his friends and nobles.
I was encouraged by the help of Yahuah my Aluahim, and I gathered men from Yasharal to go up with me.
These are the principal men, according to their fathers' houses and their groups, who went up with me from Babylon, in the reign of Artaxerxes the king:
Of the sons of Phineas, Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar, Gamaal. Of the sons of Dawiḏ, Hattush the son of Shecaniah.
Of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him a hundred and fifty men enrolled.
Of the sons of Pahathmoab, Aliehoenai the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
Of the sons of Zattu, Shecaniah the son of Jahazial, and with him three hundred men. Of the sons of Adin, Obed the son of Yahhonathan, and with him two hundred and fifty men.
Of the sons of Alam, Jeshaiah the son of Gotholiah, and with him seventy men.
Of the sons of Shephatiah, Zeraiah the son of Michaal, and with him seventy men,
Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah the son of Yahḥial, and with him two hundred and twelve men.
Of the sons of Bani, Shelomith the son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty men.
Of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah the son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
Of the sons of Azgad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten men.
Of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, their names being Aliphelet, Jeual, and Shemaiah, and with them seventy men.
Of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai the son of Istalcurus, and with him seventy men.
I assembled them at the river called Theras, and we encamped there three days, and I inspected them.
When I found there none of the sons of the kohanim or of the Levites,
I sent word to Aliezar, Idual, Maasmas,
EInathan, Shemaiah, Jarib, Nathan, EInathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, who were leaders and men of understanding;
and I told them to go to Iddo, who was the leading man at the place of the treasury,
and ordered them to tell Iddo and his brethren and the treasurers at that place to send us men to serve as kohanim in the house of our Yahuah.
And by the mighty hand of our Yahuah they brought us competent men of the sons of Mahli the son of Lewi, son of Yasharal, namely Sherebiah with his sons and kinsmen, eighteen;
also Hashabiah and Annunus and Jeshaiah his brother, of the sons of Hananiah, and their sons, twenty men;
and of the heykal servants, whom Dawiḏ and the leaders had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty heykal servants; the list of all their names was reported.
There I proclaimed a fast for the young men before our Yahuah, to seek from him a prosperous journey for ourselves and for our children and the cattle that were with us.
For I was ashamed to ask the king for foot soldiers and horsemen and an escort to keep us safe from our adversaries;
for we had said to the king, "The power of our Yahuah will be with those who seek him, and will support them in every way."
And again we prayed to our Yahuah about these things, and we found him very merciful.
Then I set apart twelve of the leaders of the kohanim, 5herebiah and Hashabiah, and ten of their kinsmen with them;
and I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the set-apart vessels of the house of our Yahuah, which the king himself and his counselors and the nobles and all Yasharal had given.
I weighed and gave to them six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and silver vessels worth a hundred talents, and a hundred talents of gold,
and twenty golden bowls, and twelve bronze vessels of fine bronze that glittered like gold.
And I said to them, "You are set-apart to Yahuah, and the vessels are set-apart, and the silver and the gold are vowed to Yahuah, Yahuah of our fathers.

Be watchful and on guard until you deliver them to the leaders of the kohanim and the Levites, and to the heads of the fathers' houses of Yasharal, in Yahrushalayim, in the chambers of the house of our Yahuah. "
So the kohanim and the Levites who took the silver and the gold and the vessels which had been in Yahrushalayim carried them to the heykal of Yahuah.

We departed from the river Theras on the twelfth day of the first month; and we arrived in Yahrushalayim by the mighty hand of our Yahuah which was upon us; he delivered us from every enemy on the way, and so we came to Yahrushalayim.
When we had been there three days, the silver and the gold were weighed and delivered in the house of our Yahuah to Meremoth the kohen, son of Uriah;
and with him was Aleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Moeth the son of Binnui, the Levites.
The whole was counted and weighed, and the weight of everything was recorded at that very time.
And those who had come back from captivity offered sacrifices to Yahuah, the Aluahim of Yasharal, twelve bulls for all Yasharal, ninety-six rams,
seventy-two lambs, and as a thank offering twelve he-goats – all as a sacrifice to Yahuah.
And they delivered the king's orders to the royal stewards and to the governors of Coelesyria and Phoenicia; and these officials honored the people and the heykal of Yahuah.
After these things had been done, the principal men came to me and said,

"The people of Yasharal and the leaders and the kohanim and the Levites have not put away from themselves the alien peoples of the land and their pollutions, the Kena'anites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Moabites, the Mitsrites, and the Edomites.

For they and their sons have married the daughters of these people, and the set-apart race has been mixed with the alien peoples of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the leaders and the nobles have been sharing in this iniquity."
As soon as I heard these things I rent my garments and my set-apart mantle, and pulled out hair from my head and beard, and sat down in anxiety and grief.
And all who were ever moved at the word of Yahuah of Yasharal gathered round me, as I mourned over this iniquity, and I sat grief-stricken until the evening sacrifice.
Then I rose from my fast, with my garments and my set-apart mantle rent, and kneeling down and stretching forth my hands to Yahuah
I said, "O Yahuah, I am ashamed and confounded before thy face.
For our sins have risen higher than our heads, and our mistakes have mounted up to shamayim
from the times of our fathers, and we are in great sin to this day.

And because of our sins and the sins of our fathers we with our brethren and our kings and our kohanim were given over to the kings of the earth, to the sword and captivity and plundering, in shame until this day.
And now in some measure mercy has come to us from thee, O Yahuah, to leave to us a root and a name in thy set-apart place,
and to uncover a light for us in the house of Yahuah our Aluahim, and to give us food in the time of our servitude.
Even in our bondage we were not forsaken by our Yahuah, but he brought us into chen with the kings of the Persians, so that they have given us food
and glorified the heykal of our Yahuah, and raised Tsiyon from desolation, to give us a stronghold in Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim.
"And now, O Yahuah, what shall we say, when we have these things? For we have transgressed thy mitsvot, which thou didst give by thy servants the neḇi'im, saying,
'The land which you are entering to take possession of it is a land polluted with the pollution of the aliens of the land, and they have filled it with their uncleanness.
Therefore do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons;
and do not seek ever to have shalom with them, in order that you may be strong and eat the good things of the land and leave it for an inheritance to your children for ever.'
And all that has happened to us has come about because of our evil deeds and our great sins. For thou, O Yahuah, didst lift the burden of our sins
and give us such a root as this; but we turned back again to transgress thy law by mixing with the uncleanness of the peoples of the land.
Wast thou not angry enough with us to destroy us without leaving a root or seed or name?
O Yahuah of Yasharal, thou art true; for we are left as a root to this day.
Behold, we are now before thee in our iniquities; for we can no longer stand in thy presence because of these things."

While Ezra was praying and making his confession, weeping and lying upon the ground before the heykal, there gathered about him a very great throng from Yahrushalayim, men and women and youths; for there was great weeping among the multitude.

Then Shecaniah the son of Yahḥial, one of the men of Yasharal, called out, and said to Ezra, "We have sinned against Yahuah, and have married foreign women from the peoples of the land; but even now there is hope for Yasharal.
Let us take an oath to Yahuah about this, that we will put away all our foreign wives, with their children,
as seems good to you and to all who obey the law of Yahuah.
Arise and take action, for it is your task, and we are with you to take strong measures."
Then Ezra arose and had the leaders of the kohanim and Levites of all Yasharal take oath that they would do this. And they took the oath.
Then Ezra rose and went from the court of the heykal to the chamber of Jehohanan the son of Aliashib,
and spent the night there; and he did not eat bread or drink water, for he was mourning over the great iniquities of the multitude.
And a proclamation was made throughout Yahuḏah and Yahrushalayim to all who had returned from the captivity that they should assemble at Yahrushalayim,

and that if any did not meet there within two or three days, in accordance with the decision of the ruling elders, their cattle should be seized for sacrifice and the men themselves expelled from the multitude of those who had returned from the captivity.
Then the men of the tribe of Yahuḏah and Binyamin assembled at Yahrushalayim within three days; this was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month.
And all the multitude sat in the open square before the heykal, shivering because of the bad weather that prevailed.
Then Ezra rose and said to them, "You have broken the law and married foreign women, and so have increased the sin of Yasharal.
Now then make confession and give glory to Yahuah the Aluahim of our fathers,
and do his will; separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from your foreign wives."
Then all the multitude shouted and said with a loud voice, "We will do as you have said.
But the multitude is great and it is winter, and we are not able to stand in the open air. This is not a work we can do in one day or two, for we have sinned too much in these things.
so let the leaders of the multitude stay, and let all those in our settlements who have foreign wives come at the time appointed,
with the elders and judges of each place, until we are freed from the wrath of Yahuah over this matter."
Yahhonathan the son of Asahal and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah undertook the matter on these terms, and Meshullam and Lewi and Shabbethai served with them as judges.
And those who had returned from the captivity acted in accordance with all this.
Ezra the kohen chose for himself the leading men of their fathers' houses, all of them by name; and on the new moon of the tenth month they began their sessions to investigate the matter.
And the cases of the men who had foreign wives were brought to an end by the new moon of the first month.
Of the kohanim those who were brought in and found to have foreign wives were:
of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brethren, Maaseiah, Aliezar, Jarib, and Jodan.
They pledged themselves to put away their wives, and to give rams in expiation of their error.
Of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah and Maaseiah and Shemaiah and Yahḥial and Azariah.
Of the sons of Pashhur: Alioenai, Maaseiah, Yahshma'al, and Nathanaal, and Gedaliah, and Alasah.
And of the Levites: Jozabad and Shimei and Kelaiah, who was Kelita, and Pethahiah and Yahuḏah and Yonah.
Of the heykal singers: Aliashib and Zaccur.
Of the gatekeepers: Shallum and Telem.
Of Yasharal: of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, and Aleazar, and Asibias, and Benaiah.
Of the sons of Alam: Mattaniah and Zechariah, Yahḥial and Abdi, and Jeremoth and Ĕliyahu.
Of the sons of Zattu: Alioenai, Aliashib, Othoniah, Jeremoth, and Zabad and Zerdaiah.
Of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan and Hananiah and Zabbai and Emathis.
Of the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Yashub, and Sheal and Jeremoth.
Of the sons of Addi: Naathus and Moossias, Laccunus and Naidus, and Bescaspasmys and Sesthal, and Belnuus and Manasseas.
Of the sons of Annan, Alionas and Asaias and Melchias and Sabbaias and Simon Chosamaeus.
Of the sons of Hashum: Mattenai and Mattattah and Zabad and Aliphelet and Menashsheh and Shimei.

Of the sons of Bani: Jeremai, Maadai, Amram, Yoal, Mamdai and Bedeiah and Vaniah, Carabasion and Aliashib and Machnadebai, Aliasis, Binnui, Alialis, Shimei, Shelemiah, Nethaniah. Of the sons of Ezora: Shashai, Azaral, Azaal, Shemaiah, Amariah, Yoseph.
Of the sons of Nebo: Mattithiah, Zabad, Iddo, Yoal, Benaiah.
All these had married foreign women, and they put them away with their children.
The kohanim and the Levites and the men of Yasharal settled in Yahrushalayim and in the country. On the new moon of the seventh month, when the sons of Yasharal were in their settlements,
the whole multitude gathered with one accord into the open square before the east gate of the heykal;
and they told Ezra the chief kohen and reader to bring the law of Mosheh which had been given by Yahuah Aluahim of Yasharal.
So Ezra the chief kohen brought the law, for all the multitude, men and women, and all the kohanim to hear the law, on the new moon of the seventh month.
And he read aloud in the open square before the gate of the heykal from early morning until midday, in the presence of both men and women; and all the multitude gave attention to the law.
Ezra the kohen and reader of the law stood on the wooden platform which had been prepared;
and beside him stood Mattathiah, Shema, Anaiah, Azariah, Uriah, Hezekiah, and Baalsamus on his right hand,
and on his left Pedaiah, Mishaal, Malchijah, Lothasubus, Nabariah, and Zechariah.
Then Ezra took up the book of the law in the sight of the multitude, for he had the place of honor in the presence of all.
And when he opened the law, they all stood erect. And Ezra baruk Yahuah Aluahim Most High, the Aluahim of hosts, the Almighty;
and all the multitude answered, "Amen." And they lifted up their hands, and fell to the ground and worshiped Yahuah.

Jeshua and Anniuth and Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah and Kelita, Azariah and Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, the Levites, taught the law of Yahuah, at the same time explaining what was read.
Then Attharates said to Ezra the chief kohen and reader, and to the Levites who were teaching the multitude, and to all,
"This day is set-apart to Yahuah" – now they were all weeping as they heard the law –
"so go your way, eat the fat and drink the sweet, and send portions to those who have none;
for the day is set-apart to Yahuah; and do not be sorrowful, for Yahuah will exalt you."
And the Levites commanded all the people, saying, "This day is set-apart; do not be sorrowful."
Then they all went their way, to eat and drink and enjoy themselves, and to give portions to those who had none, and to make great rejoicing;
because they were inspired by the words which they had been taught. And they came together.
